routes.why: The smallest change that finishes the job. Leave validation, error handling, security, and accessibility in place.
Read it like someone who gets paged.
That same pass, over every file.

routes.when: Shortcuts you meant to come back to

items.name: grill-me
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: They asked to grill a plan or design, or the ask is underspecified
items.why: Interview until every branch of the design tree is resolved. Uses grilling. A feature goes on to to-spec, then to-tickets.

items.name: grilling
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Stress-testing a plan, decision, or idea
items.why: The interview primitive behind grill-me. Relentless questions until branches are closed.

items.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Before to-spec or to-tickets in a repo with no tracker set up
items.why: Once per repo. Picks where specs and tickets live: GitHub Issues when the repo is on GitHub, else local markdown. Writes its `## Agent skills` block outside the longbeard markers.

items.name: to-spec
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: A grilled feature to write down whole
items.why: One spec on the tracker setup chose: problem, user stories, decisions, test seams, out of scope. No tracker set up yet: run setup-matt-pocock-skills first. A small feature can skip it and go to to-tickets.

items.name: to-tickets
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: A spec, plan, or conversation to split into tickets
items.why: Vertical slices, each checkable on its own, with their blockers, on the tracker setup chose. No tracker set up yet: run setup-matt-pocock-skills first.

items.name: implement
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Building one ticket, or a spec in one session
items.why: Read the ticket from the tracker, build it with tdd at the seams the spec agreed, then code-review, then commit.

items.name: implement-spec
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Building every ticket of a spec
items.why: One integration branch. A fresh agent per ticket in its own worktree, each with tdd, started as its blockers finish. code-review at the end.

items.name: tdd
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: They asked for TDD, test-first, or red-green-refactor
items.why: Red before green, one slice at a time, tests at seams you agreed. implement and implement-spec call it. Otherwise only on request; ponytail stays the default for building.

items.name: code-review
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Reviewing work built from a spec or ticket
items.why: Two axes, in parallel: this repo's standards, and the spec. A plain diff stays ponytail-review.

items.name: diagnosing-bugs
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Something is broken, throwing, failing, or slow — a hard bug
items.why: Build a tight feedback loop first, then localize, reduce, fix, and guard.

items.name: prototype
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: A throwaway prototype of logic or state
items.why: A page or screen goes to design-taste-frontend.

items.name: improve-codebase-architecture
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Deepening modules or the shape of the code
items.why: Uses codebase-design and domain-modeling. Bugs, load, and bloat across the repo stay ponytail-audit.

items.name: codebase-design
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Designing a module's interface
items.why: The shared vocabulary for deep modules that improve-codebase-architecture uses.

items.name: domain-modeling
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Naming the project's terms or recording a decision
items.why: Keeps `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs current, created only when a term or decision is settled. improve-codebase-architecture calls it.

items.name: handoff
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: They asked to hand off to another agent or session
items.why: Compact the conversation into a handoff document another agent can pick up.

items.name: retro
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: They asked for a retro on a session
items.why: Find what would have made the session easier: checks, navigation pointers, review rules, tool cost. Uses writing-for-agents. Suggests; you choose.

items.name: writing-for-agents
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Writing a skill, AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md
items.why: The style guide retro uses.

items.name: premortem
items.author: GeorgeT
items.when: A change that touches data, money, jobs, or what a person sees
items.why: Name where it can break before you write. A small change gets a short answer.

items.name: design-reference-hunt
items.author: Long Beard
items.when: No official look, or they asked to hunt / define direction / find references
items.why: Does not code the page. Talk first, one round, then search small. Pick on `.design/moodboard.html`, say the adaptation, then ask to write or update `DESIGN.md` via design-md as its own message — once more, first, if they move on without answering — only on yes. Then offer the next step: prototype the gaps, hunt one, or stop. A later hunt for one piece writes `.design/hunts/<slug>/`. `.design/` is scratch, out of git.

items.name: design-taste-frontend
items.author: Leonxlnx
items.when: They asked to build, code, or prototype a page or screen
items.why: With DESIGN.md it builds and checks; it does not art-direct: no draw, no dealt references, palette, or type. Else build from the `.design/board.md` cards. Run `inspect.mjs` (`--app` and its app-screen house rules for an app screen). Report a warning about something DESIGN.md decides as per DESIGN.md; contrast, focus, and tap-target failures still get fixed. Direction-only or hunt-only is not this skill. The control a card describes is the control; add no filled button it does not show.

items.name: animate
items.author: emilkowalski
items.when: They asked to animate a control or a transition
items.why: Read the Behaviour section of DESIGN.md first. A page design-taste-frontend is building keeps that skill’s motion. Decide this one move, then build it.

items.name: figma-design-to-code
items.author: Figma
items.when: A Figma file or link
items.why: A designer handed it over. Needs the Figma connection. Reuse this project's components.

items.name: image-to-code
items.author: Leonxlnx
items.when: A picture you already have
items.why: Build the page from that picture.

items.name: security-audit
items.author: Cloudflare
items.when: A security review you asked for
items.why: Look for a broken trust boundary. The full audit runs only when you ask for an audit or a pen-test.

items.name: web-design-guidelines
items.author: Vercel
items.when: A UI review you asked for
items.why: Accessibility and interface rules.

items.name: jury
items.author: juliobsz
items.when: They asked to jury, score, judge, or roast the design (or a live URL / local build)
items.why: Blind evidence scorecard. Do not redesign. Fixes stay on the board, DESIGN.md, or Figma. Do not run after every build unless they asked.

items.name: design-md
items.author: Long Beard
items.when: The look of this project, or they confirmed writing or updating DESIGN.md
items.why: Follow DESIGN.md when it exists. Write or update it only on confirm: from the hunt's adaptation, or from decisions approved on a rendered prototype, with reason, date, and contrast. Ideas, not sources: no reference names or `.design/` paths. Do not invent. Missing file plus design or define direction is hunt first.
